turns.speaker: A

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: A

turns.text: Thanks so much for making time, Elena. How did you end up as a product manager at Lumen Health?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I was a nurse for six years first. I kept seeing nurses fight the charting software at three in the morning, and at some point I decided I'd rather fix it than complain about it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a big jump. I'm actually really interested in health tech too, I've been building an app for my research lab that tracks sleep data, and I'm hoping to find an internship where I can do something like that.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Nice. What does the app do with the data?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It flags nights when students sleep under five hours before an exam. What was the hardest part of going from nursing to product?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Learning to say no. Nurses say yes to everything because someone's health depends on it. In product, if you say yes to everything, nothing ships.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Learning to say no, I like that. How do you decide what to say no to?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I ask whether it helps the nurse at three in the morning. If it doesn't, it waits. I'm actually presenting that framework at a conference in two weeks, in Denver.

turns.speaker: A

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ruthless for the night shift. My manager hates the title, so I'm keeping it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Please do. And send me your resume, I'll pass it to our intern lead.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hola Mamá, ¿cómo están todos?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Bien, mija, un poco nerviosa. La cirugía de tu papá es el próximo martes, la de la rodilla, y ya sabes cómo se pone él con los hospitales.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ay, yo también tengo mucho estrés con la escuela, tengo tres proyectos esta semana y no he dormido nada.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ay, mija, no te estreses. ¿Estás comiendo bien?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Sí, sí. Oye, ¿y papá qué dice de la cirugía? ¿Tiene miedo?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Dice que no, pero anoche no durmió. Le preguntó al doctor una y otra vez cuánto tiempo va a estar sin manejar. Para él no manejar es como no tener piernas.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: ¿Cuánto tiempo va a estar sin manejar?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Seis semanas. Ya le dije que yo lo llevo a todos lados, pero él quiere que lo lleve tu tío porque según él yo manejo como taxista.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Jaja, sí manejas como taxista. ¿Quieres que vaya a casa el fin de semana después de la cirugía para ayudar?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ay, sí mija, eso le alegraría mucho. Y a mí también.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Te llamo el martes después de la cirugía.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Gracias, mi amor. Cuídate mucho y come algo, ¿eh?

conversations.reflection: I made her nerves about me for a second. Asked about papá after.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So? How did the Verdant interview go?!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I think it went well? The whiteboard part was actually fine because we practiced. I drew the forecasting pipeline and didn't freeze once.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You didn't freeze once! What did they ask you to design?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A system that predicts solar output for every rooftop in Austin. I started with the weather data like you said, and the interviewer literally said that is how their team does it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Wait, the interviewer said that is how their team does it? That has to be a good sign.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Maybe. The recruiter said I'll hear back about the final step tomorrow. I'm trying not to refresh my email every five minutes.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's so exciting. What happens in the final step?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Lunch with the team lead. Which is scarier than the whiteboard honestly, I never know what to talk about at those.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ask the team lead about their favorite forecasting failure, people love telling those. And I'll grab you a coffee tomorrow morning so you're not refreshing alone.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Deal. Thank you for the practice, seriously. It made a difference.

conversations.reflection: This felt like the best one. I remembered everything from last time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hola Abuela! I've been thinking about the mole since you told me about the metate. ¿Me enseñas la receta?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: ¡Claro que sí! But it is not a recipe, mija, it is a whole day. Twenty-six ingredients, and the chiles have to be toasted until the whole house smells like smoke.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Twenty-six ingredients? Which chile is the hardest to get here?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The chilhuacle negro. You can only find it in Oaxaca, so Lupe brings it in her suitcase. She's coming next month, for Día de Muertos.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Tía Lupe is coming for Día de Muertos? Will you make the altar together?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sí, every year we put the altar for my mother and father. Pan de muerto, cempasúchil, and a little cup of mezcal for my father because he would be angry without it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A cup of mezcal for your father, I love that. What was he like?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Stubborn like your papá. He sold corn in the market in Oaxaca and he knew every family by name. When he laughed the whole market could hear it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'll bring the pan de muerto for the altar this year. Can you teach me how to put the cempasúchil on the altar?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ay, mija, sí. Your great-grandfather would be so proud.

conversations.reflection: I finally asked about the mole like the app told me weeks ago. Best call in a while.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hi Daniel, thanks again for passing my resume along. How have things been on the warehouse team?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Busy. We're rolling out the new picking arm to the Dallas warehouse next week, so everyone is living in the test cell right now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The new arm, is that the one that handles the crushed boxes?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's the one. It catches about nine out of ten now. The last ten percent is the fun part, it's all the weird stuff like shrink wrap that reflects the depth camera.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Shrink wrap reflects the depth camera? How do you even collect data on that?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We built a little cart we call the junk drawer. It's full of the worst packages we've ever seen and we run it past the arm every night. Honestly it's my favorite part of the job.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The junk drawer is such a good name. Would an intern get to work on that?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Probably, yes. The recruiter told me your first interview is next Thursday, so ask them about the failure lab, they'll be impressed you know about it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I will. I'll send you a thank you note after the interview and tell you how it went.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sounds good. And don't over-prepare, just talk about the satellite project like you did at the booth.

conversations.reflection: Way better than the career fair. I asked about his stuff first.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You finished! How was the race?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Two hours and three minutes. I wanted under two, but my mom watched the livestream from her chemo chair and texted me the whole time, so honestly it was perfect.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Your mom texted you from the chemo chair? What did she say?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Mostly 'run faster' in all caps. And at mile ten she sent a picture of the nurses holding up a sign with my name on it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The nurses made a sign? I am going to cry. Did you decide about Seattle?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'm taking it. But I asked them to let me start in March so I can be in Houston for her last rounds of treatment, and they said yes.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: They said yes to March, that's amazing. How are you feeling about it now?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Relieved. Scared too. I keep thinking about leaving the running group, they're kind of my people here.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What if we do one last long run with the running group before you go? I'll find a route and send it to you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. Something with tacos at the end.

conversations.reflection: So happy for her. I want to ask more about the running group next time.
